The test image shows a tomato leaf with:
- Yellowing/chlorosis along the upper leaf margin
- Brown necrotic tissue at the leaf tip/margin (dried, dead tissue)
- The yellowing forms a wedge/V-shaped pattern widest at the margin, tapering inward
- Small dark lesions within the yellowed area
- Green tissue remaining in the lower leaf portions

This V-shaped margin pattern strongly suggests **Verticillium Wilt**. Let me check one reference image.

The reference confirms the pattern. The Verticillium Wilt reference shows yellowing/wilting leaves, and the test image clearly demonstrates the classic V-shaped necrosis widest at the leaf margin with brown necrotic tissue surrounded by irregular yellowing — exactly matching the symptom description: "V-shaped leaf lesions widest at the leaf margin, brown necrotic tissue surrounded by irregular yellowing."
